**Figure 4-3**  Auto generated code from Student class diagram

Using the Class Diagram tool in Visual Studio gives you the added benefit of graphically viewing the class. You can define the class template for the class just using the code editor as was done with previous application. However, if you use the Class Diagram tool you can also switch back and forth between the class diagram and the code window. Each has a separate tab. You’ll notice in Figure 4–2 that the file that holds the class diagram has a .cd extension.

Figure 4–3 illustrated where the fields or data members (instance variables) are declared. As illustrated in Examples 4–1 and 4–2, data fields are normally declared first inside the body of the **class** definition. In the examples that follow, the CarpetCalculator, from Chapter 3, is revisited using an object-oriented approach.
